newsitem.title: CANADA: Ethyl to claim compensation for MMT ban.
newsitem.headline: Ethyl to claim compensation for MMT ban.

text.p: Ethyl Corp said on Thursday it would make good on its threat to seek compensation from the Canadian government for the impact of Canada's new ban on gas additive MMT.
The Virginia-based company said it would file a claim for compensation under the North American Free Trade Agreement. Ethyl said previously it would seek US$200 million in damages.
Ethyl's statement came a day after the Canadian Senate passed Bill C-29, which would ban the import and interprovincial trade of MMT.
Ethyl's Canadian subsidiary supplies the Canadian market with the additive, methylcyclopentadienyl manganese tricarbonyl, and loses its principal market with the passage of the bill.

"Nafta, as approved by Parliament, is now being violated by the same legislature with passage of C-29," Ethyl spokesman Chris Hicks said in a statement. "Ethyl and our shareholders have been harmed by the unfounded comments and actions by certain individuals in the Canadian government."
MMT boosts octane in gasoline, but the Liberal government argues it hurts the environment and health of Canadians.
The government also says MMT gums up car parts.
But Ethyl Corp and the bill's critics have said there was no scientific basis for the Liberals' claims.
The province of Alberta has also said it would take legal action to oppose the new law.
